sentences.en: We have lots of ways to describe the good that can sometimes come from bad.
sentences.zh: 我们有许多方法来描述有时可能由坏事带来的好事。

sentences.en: A blessing in disguise, a silver lining.
sentences.zh: 塞翁失马，祸福相依。

sentences.en: But what if the bad that led to the good was truly awful?
sentences.zh: 但如果导致好事的坏事本身极其糟糕呢？

sentences.en: You could see that his face was starting to balloon to a size where I realized how bad it was that he had gotten hurt.
sentences.zh: 你能看出他的脸开始肿得像个气球，让我意识到他受的伤有多严重。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是“隐藏大脑”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: There's really just one way to look at a given event.
sentences.zh: 对于某个特定的事件，其实通常只有一种看法。

sentences.en: A slight change in outcome can change the way we see and interpret an experience.
sentences.zh: 结果的微小变化可以改变我们看待和解读经历的方式。

sentences.en: This week, we have the story of three people who discover that an event they initially viewed as terrible might in fact have been just the opposite.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们为您讲述三个人的故事，他们发现某个最初被视为可怕的事件，事实上可能恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Not awful, but a stroke of unimaginable good luck.
sentences.zh: 不是糟糕，而是一场难以想象的好运。

sentences.en: Framing and reframing, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 界定与重新界定，本周“隐藏大脑”。

sentences.en: December 21st is the winter solstice, the shortest day of the year.
sentences.zh: 12月21日是冬至，一年中白天最短的一天。

sentences.en: It's also the day our story begins.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们故事开始的日子。

sentences.en: Three people have finished work.
sentences.zh: 三个人结束了工作。

sentences.en: Each is heading to a metro train station in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 每个人都正前往华盛顿特区的一个地铁站。

sentences.en: And it was just before rush hour.
sentences.zh: 当时正值晚高峰前夕。

sentences.en: I was planning to meet my wife, who works a few stations ahead of me.
sentences.zh: 我当时正计划去见我妻子，她在离我前几站的地方工作。

sentences.en: This is Colin Dale.
sentences.zh: 这是科林·戴尔。

sentences.en: He's at the center of our story.
sentences.zh: 他是我们故事的核心人物。

sentences.en: Colin is 42, happily married.
sentences.zh: 科林42岁，婚姻美满。

sentences.en: He's got two teenage kids and a successful job as a technology consultant.
sentences.zh: 他有两个十几岁的孩子，并且是一名成功的技术顾问。

sentences.en: He's also, as you can hear, originally from England.
sentences.zh: 正如你所听到的，他原本也是英国人。

sentences.en: Colin was the first person in our story to reach the station and board a train.
sentences.zh: 科林是我们故事中第一个到达车站并登上列车的人。

sentences.en: And that's where the trouble started.
sentences.zh: 麻烦就是从那里开始的。

sentences.en: I do vaguely remember that a group of youths got on the train.
sentences.zh: 我隐约记得有一群年轻人上了车。

sentences.en: And I must have thought that they were being somehow rambunctious or aggressive.
sentences.zh: 我当时一定觉得他们有些吵闹或具有攻击性。

sentences.en: Because I remember texting my wife in a panic, really, to be honest with you, don't get on the train.
sentences.zh: 因为我记得自己曾惊慌失措地给妻子发信息，老实说，别上这趟车。

sentences.en: Another woman did get on the train with Colin.
sentences.zh: 另一位女士也和科林一起上了车。

sentences.en: Her name is Kristen Smith.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫克里斯滕·史密斯。

sentences.en: Kristen had made a dash for the train and jumped into the first car, the same one in which Colin was riding.
sentences.zh: 克里斯滕一路小跑冲向列车，跳进了第一节车厢，也就是科林乘坐的那节车厢。

sentences.en: I could tell as soon as I had jumped in that it was a weird situation.
sentences.zh: 我一跳上车就看得出来情况有点不对劲。

sentences.en: I felt uncomfortable as soon as I got through the doors.
sentences.zh: 我一进车门就感到浑身不自在。

sentences.en: The first thing she noticed was a group of boisterous teenagers.
sentences.zh: 她注意到的第一件事是一群喧闹的青少年。

sentences.en: It felt like there were a lot of kids in all four seats that surround that middle door of the subway car.
sentences.zh: 感觉地铁车厢中间车门周围的所有四个座位上都坐满了年轻人。

sentences.en: And there were also kids standing in the aisle in a way where it was clear they weren't going to make room for people coming on or off.
sentences.zh: 还有一些年轻人站在过道里，明显不会给上下车的人腾出空间。

sentences.en: You had to make your way around them.
sentences.zh: 你必须绕过他们才能通过。

sentences.en: I'm Lori Kaplan, and I head up the Audience Insights Department at NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是洛里·卡普兰，我负责美国国家公共电台的观众洞察部。

sentences.en: This is Colin's wife.
sentences.zh: 这是科林的妻子。

sentences.en: She's a colleague of mine.
sentences.zh: 她我的同事。

sentences.en: Lori had timed her departure from work so she'd arrive at her metro station just before Colin's train pulled in.
sentences.zh: 洛里计算好了离开工作的时间，以便在科林的列车进站前到达她的地铁站。

sentences.en: As I was approaching the platform, I texted him to say,
sentences.zh: 当我走近月台时，我发信息告诉他，

sentences.en: I'm here.
sentences.zh: 我到了。

sentences.en: I'm here.
sentences.zh: 我到了。

sentences.en: I'm almost here.
sentences.zh: 我快到了。

sentences.en: And he said, don't get on.
sentences.zh: 他说，别上车。

sentences.en: And I had seen these text messages that arrived during my walk that said,
sentences.zh: 我看到了在我步行时收到的那些短信，上面写着，

sentences.en: don't get on the first train, because we normally get on the first car of the train.
sentences.zh: 别上第一列车，因为我们通常坐列车的节车厢。

sentences.en: What happens next, on the train and in the days that follow, is what our story is about.
sentences.zh: 接下来在列车上以及随后的几天里发生的事情，就是我们这个故事的主题。

sentences.en: It's a tragic story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个悲惨的故事。

sentences.en: But perhaps it's also a story of profound luck.
sentences.zh: 但也许这也是一个充满巨大运气的传奇。

sentences.en: It all depends on how you frame it,
sentences.zh: 这一切都取决于你如何看待它，

sentences.en: the lens through which you view what happened.
sentences.zh: 也就是你审视所发生事情的视角。

sentences.en: Let me start by going back a bit into the lives of Colin and Lori.
sentences.zh: 让我先回溯一下科林和洛里的生活。

sentences.en: The two first met when the company Colin worked for was hired by NPR for a contract project.
sentences.zh: 两人初次相遇时，科林工作的公司被美国国家公共电台雇佣为一个合同项目。

sentences.en: It wasn't going well.
sentences.zh: 当时进展并不顺利。

sentences.en: The person who was leading that work said,
sentences.zh: 负责那项工作的人说，

sentences.en: I am going to Idaho, but if you have any problems, call this guy Colin.
sentences.zh: 我要去爱达荷州，但如果你们遇到任何问题，给这个叫科林的家伙打电话。

sentences.en: He'll help you out.
sentences.zh: 他会帮你们解决的。

sentences.en: In fact, the project was a mess.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那个项目简直一团糟。

sentences.en: So Lori called.
sentences.zh: 于是洛里打了电话。

sentences.en: She was really mad.
sentences.zh: 她当时非常生气。

sentences.en: Yelling.
sentences.zh: 在大喊大叫。

sentences.en: I was quite unpleasant, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实我当时态度挺不友好的。

sentences.en: But he fixed the problem, and he's been fixing a lot of my problems ever since.
sentences.zh: 但他解决了问题，从那以后他一直在帮我解决很多问题。

sentences.en: Eventually, they got married, had children.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们结婚了，有了孩子。

sentences.en: Lori describes Colin this way.
sentences.zh: 洛里这样描述科林。

sentences.en: He's calm.
sentences.zh: 他很冷静。

sentences.en: He cares.
sentences.zh: 他在乎。

sentences.en: He cares a lot.
sentences.zh: 他非常在乎。

sentences.en: He's a great dad.
sentences.zh: 他是个好爸爸。

sentences.en: I think all he ever wanted to be was probably a dad.
sentences.zh: 我想他这辈子唯一想当的可能就是一个父亲。

sentences.en: He is a fixer and a doer, and I'm a doer, so we just do a lot of things together.
sentences.zh: 他是一个解决问题的人也是一个行动派，而我也是个行动派，所以我们经常一起做很多事。

sentences.en: They're both athletic, especially Colin.
sentences.zh: 他们都很热爱运动，尤其是科林。

sentences.en: From his childhood, he used to bike all over the north of England.
sentences.zh: 从小时候起，他就常在英格兰北部到处骑自行车。

sentences.en: That's just what he would do.
sentences.zh: 他就是这样的人。

sentences.en: So he grew up biking, and he was a Boy Scout leader and would kayak, and so he was very active.
sentences.zh: 所以他是骑着车长大的，曾担任童子军领袖，还会玩皮划艇，因此他非常活跃。

sentences.en: And then when he moved here, he would bike to work from our house to D.C.
sentences.zh: 后来他搬到这里后，每周会有很多次从我们家骑车去华盛顿特区上班。

sentences.en: many times a week.
sentences.zh: 很多次每周。

sentences.en: And, yeah, we hiked with our family, too, so he was very active.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，我们全家也会一起徒步旅行，所以他非常活跃。

sentences.en: You might have noticed that Lori said Colin was very active.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经注意到洛里说科林非常活跃。

sentences.en: That's because in the last couple of years, he'd been having some trouble.
sentences.zh: 那是因为在过去几年里，他遇到了一些麻烦。

sentences.en: He was having a lot of joint pain and discomfort, and it was just his knees hurt, his arms hurt, his legs hurt.
sentences.zh: 他有许多关节疼痛和不适，具体来说就是他的膝盖疼、胳膊疼、腿疼。

sentences.en: He just had a lot of pain, and so it just made it challenging to bike because it was very uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 他身上有各种疼痛，这让骑车变得很有挑战性，因为很不舒服。

sentences.en: But it was challenging to walk, frankly.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，走路也很困难。

sentences.en: He would stop sometimes on the way to the metro, which felt really unusual to me.
sentences.zh: 有时他在去地铁的路上会停下来，这让我觉得非常不寻常。

sentences.en: Colin had tried to figure out what was wrong.
sentences.zh: 科林曾试图找出问题所在。

sentences.en: He'd seen a lot of doctors, a lot of specialists.
sentences.zh: 他看过很多医生，许多专家。

sentences.en: Everyone was stumped.
sentences.zh: 所有人都束手无策。

sentences.en: Colin was frustrated.
sentences.zh: 科林感到很沮丧。

sentences.en: And so when he stepped onto the train that evening, shortly before Christmas,
sentences.zh: 因此，当他在圣诞节前不久的那个晚上踏上列车时，

sentences.en: he was taking a break from his quest for an answer.
sentences.zh: 他正在暂停寻找答案的探寻。

sentences.en: Colin would like to be able to explain what happened on that train ride, but he can't.
sentences.zh: 科林很希望能解释那天在列车上发生了什么，但他做不到。

sentences.en: After texting his wife, his memories of the ride are gone.
sentences.zh: 在给妻子发完短信后，他对那次乘车过程的记忆已经消失了。

sentences.en: Kristen Smith, on the other hand, has been haunted by memories of that commute.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，克里斯滕·史密斯一直被那次通勤的记忆所困扰。

sentences.en: She says she took a seat and leaned her head up against the window.
sentences.zh: 她说她找了个座位坐下，把头靠在窗户上。

sentences.en: I have tried to think a lot about what it was that made me turn around, and I can't quite remember.
sentences.zh: 我曾试图去回想究竟是什么让我转过身去，但我记不太清了。

sentences.en: But I think it was either a period of awkward silence, or I heard scuffling,
sentences.zh: 但我认为要么是一段尴尬的沉默，要么是我听到了争执声，

sentences.en: and that made me turn around to look back at the middle of the car.
sentences.zh: 这让我转过身去查看车厢中间的情况。

sentences.en: Kristen says it was hard to tell exactly what was happening,
sentences.zh: 克里斯滕说很难确切说出当时发生了什么，

sentences.en: but she could see that the group of teenagers was surrounding one man.
sentences.zh: 但她能看到那群青少年正围着一个男人。

sentences.en: And he had a blue backpack, and I remember he had his arms up through the backpack straps
sentences.zh: 他背着一个蓝色双背包，我记得他的手臂穿过了背包带，

sentences.en: with the backpack facing up, and he was shielding himself.
sentences.zh: 背包朝上，他在保护自己。

sentences.en: He was using the blue backpack as a shield.
sentences.zh: 他正用那个蓝色双肩包当盾牌。

sentences.en: It was Colin Dale.
sentences.zh: 那是科林·戴尔。

sentences.en: Kristen says he tried to get away.
sentences.zh: 克里斯滕说他试图逃跑。

sentences.en: And as he took a step, he got hit in rapid succession, I thought he got hit in rapid succession
sentences.zh: 当他迈出一步时，他接连遭到击打，我以为他接连挨了

sentences.en: with maybe two hits, and he fell down to the ground.
sentences.zh: 大约两下攻击，然后他倒在了地上。

sentences.en: And then the kids all stepped away from him.
sentences.zh: 接着那些孩子都从他身边退开了。

sentences.en: And in my mind, that felt like a good thing, that the kids had stepped,
sentences.zh: 在我的脑海里，我觉得这是一件好事，孩子们退开了，

sentences.en: or that the youths had stepped away from him, and that it had stopped,
sentences.zh: 或者说那些年轻人从他身边退开，事情已经停下来了，

sentences.en: like the violence had stopped in that moment.
sentences.zh: 就像那一刻暴力已经停止了一样。

sentences.en: And I think that was my first thought, was just relief,
sentences.zh: 我想我当时的第一反应只是感到宽慰，

sentences.en: that maybe this would stop and they'd leave him alone now.
sentences.zh: 也许这会停下来，他们现在会离他远点。

sentences.en: But I didn't realize that he was in such bad shape at that point.
sentences.zh: 但我当时并没有意识到他已经伤得那么重。

sentences.en: I could see his feet sticking out from the, between the metro car seats out into the aisle.
sentences.zh: 我能看到他的脚从地铁座位之间伸出来，伸到了过道里。

sentences.en: Colin eventually got up and staggered toward Kristen and another commuter.
sentences.zh: 科林最终站了起来，踉踉跄跄地朝克里斯滕和另一名乘客走去。

sentences.en: They tried to comfort him.
sentences.zh: 他们试图安慰他。

sentences.en: The train was nearing Lori Station.
sentences.zh: 列车正在接近洛里的车站。

sentences.en: Kristen says without drawing the attention of the teenagers,
sentences.zh: 克里斯滕说，在不引起青少年注意的情况下，

sentences.en: she tried to let the conductor know what was going on.
sentences.zh: 她试图让列车员知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: And there's a little crack between the door and where the door connects to the wall, I guess.
sentences.zh: 车门和车门连接墙壁的地方似乎有一条小缝隙。

sentences.en: And I started saying through the door crack, you have to, you have to stop the train,
sentences.zh: 我开始透过门缝说，你必须，你必须停下列车，

sentences.en: you have to get medical help, you have to get the police, there's an attack.
sentences.zh: 你必须寻求医疗援助，你必须叫警察，这里发生袭击了。

sentences.en: It worked.
sentences.zh: 这管用了。

sentences.en: When the train came to a stop at the station, the doors to Colin's car remained closed.
sentences.zh: 当列车在车站停下时，科林所在车厢的车门保持紧闭。

sentences.en: The teenagers panicked.
sentences.zh: 青少年们惊慌失措。

sentences.en: And that's when they turned, and there are emergency exit doors at the end of the car,
sentences.zh: 就在那时他们转过身去，车厢尽头有紧急安全出口门，

sentences.en: which would have been at the end of the car away from me.
sentences.zh: 那应该是在离我较远的车厢另一端。

sentences.en: And they all turned, and they ran down and went through the exit door of the car.
sentences.zh: 他们全都转过身，跑过去穿过了车厢的紧急出口门。

sentences.en: Lori, meanwhile, was on the escalator.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，洛里正在自动扶梯上。

sentences.en: When she reached the platform, she saw that the train had been unloaded.
sentences.zh: 当她到达月台时，她看到列车上的人已经全部下车了。

sentences.en: I just looked around.
sentences.zh: 我只是四处张望。

sentences.en: He should be here.
sentences.zh: 他应该在这里的。

sentences.en: So I walked further down the platform, even though he said he was going to get off the first car.
sentences.zh: 所以我沿着月台继续往前走，尽管他说过他要从第一节车厢下车。

sentences.en: I walked all the way to the front, and that was the only train car that was closed.
sentences.zh: 我一直走到最前面，那是唯一一节关闭的车厢。

sentences.en: The train doors were shut, and then I saw Colin on the train.
sentences.zh: 列车门是关着的，然后我看到了车上的科林。

sentences.en: He looked terrible.
sentences.zh: 他看起来糟透了。

sentences.en: He looked like a ghoSt.
sentences.zh: 他看起来像个鬼魂。

sentences.en: I saw blood on his face, and he started hitting the glass on the front of the conductor's car,
sentences.zh: 我看到他脸上有血迹，他开始敲击列车长室前方的玻璃，

sentences.en: the driver's car, saying, that's my wife, that's my wife.
sentences.zh: 也就是司机室，嘴里说，那是我妻子，那是我妻子。

sentences.en: And they let me on the train, and I took him off the train, and I sat him down on a bench.
sentences.zh: 他们让我上了车，我把他扶下列车，让他坐在一张长椅上。

sentences.en: It was a little bench near the end of the platform.
sentences.zh: 那是月台尽头附近的一个小长椅。

sentences.en: And I put his head down because I saw he was bleeding.
sentences.zh: 我把他的头放低，因为我看到他在流血。

sentences.en: Immediately, one of the metro police officers approached me, and he said,
sentences.zh: 一名地铁警察立刻向我走来，他说，

sentences.en: we have an ambulance on the way.
sentences.zh: 我们的救护车正在路上。

sentences.en: Colin was in very bad shape.
sentences.zh: 科林的情况非常糟糕。

sentences.en: His teeth were shattered.
sentences.zh: 他的牙齿碎了。

sentences.en: His jaw jutted out to one side like he'd stuffed a balloon into his cheek.
sentences.zh: 他的下巴向一边歪去，就像嘴里塞了一个气球一样。

sentences.en: He was disoriented.
sentences.zh: 他神志不清。

sentences.en: He kept asking the same questions over and over again.
sentences.zh: 他不停地反反复复问着同样的问题。

sentences.en: He would ask me, was there, was I in an accident on my bike?
sentences.zh: 他会问我，当时是不是，我是不是骑自行车出了事故？

sentences.en: Was there a terrorist attack?
sentences.zh: 是不是发生了恐怖袭击？

sentences.en: Was there, like, what happened?
sentences.zh: 是不是，比方说，到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: He didn't know, but he would just look and assess the situation and ask me.
sentences.zh: 他并不知道，但他只是看着并评估情况，然后问我。

sentences.en: And then he would ask if I was okay.
sentences.zh: 接着他会问我有没有事。

sentences.en: Even when he saw the ambulance, he thought maybe something was happening to me.
sentences.zh: 甚至当他看到救护车时，他还以为我是出了什么事。

sentences.en: At the hospital, a team of doctors took over.
sentences.zh: 到了医院，一组医生接手了治疗。

sentences.en: As soon as he was admitted, they realized he was complaining of neck probleMs.
sentences.zh: 他刚一入院，他们就发现他一直在抱怨脖子有问题。

sentences.en: And so they immediately, that evening, had done CAT scans and then MRI, a series of MRIs.
sentences.zh: 于是他们当晚立刻做了CT扫描，然后是核磁共振，一连串的核磁共振。

sentences.en: And this is where our story takes a turn.
sentences.zh: 我们的故事就在这里发生了转折。

sentences.en: Up to this point, I think most of us would agree that what happened to Colin was terrible.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，我想我们大多数人都会同意，科林遭遇的事情太可怕了。

sentences.en: An unprovoked, brutal attack that left him badly injured and his wife, children, and witnesses traumatized.
sentences.zh: 这是一场毫无挑衅、残忍至极的袭击，让他身受重伤，他的妻子、孩子和目击者们也受到了极大的创伤。

sentences.en: It's hard to frame the incident any other way.
sentences.zh: 很难用其他方式来解读这起事件。

sentences.en: But what comes next may change your mind.
sentences.zh: 但接下来发生的事可能会改变你的想法。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: After a brutal assault on a D.C.
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿特区

sentences.en: metro train, Colin Dale is in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 地铁列车上发生残忍的袭击后，科林·戴尔住进了医院。

sentences.en: Surgeons are preparing to repair his jaw with a titanium plate.
sentences.zh: 外科医生正准备用钛板修复他的下巴。

sentences.en: He's wearing a brace for neck pain and waiting for scan results to figure out whether the attack caused any further harm.
sentences.zh: 他戴着颈托缓解颈部疼痛，并等待扫描结果，以确定袭击是否造成了进一步的伤害。

sentences.en: Colin says a doctor walked into the room.
sentences.zh: 科林说，有个医生走进了病房。

sentences.en: Someone, you know, he's wearing a blue outfit, looked like he fit in a hospital,
sentences.zh: 有个家伙，你知道的，穿着一身蓝色衣服，看起来就像个医院的人，

sentences.en: came by my bed with a printout of the MRI.
sentences.zh: 拿着核磁共振打印件来到了我的床边。

sentences.en: And I'd had a neck brace on, and he said, well, you know, Mr. Dale, you can take the neck brace off.
sentences.zh: 当时我戴着颈托，他说，嗯，你知道的，戴尔先生，你可以把颈托摘下来了。

sentences.en: But I just want to show you this part on the MRI.
sentences.zh: 但我只是想让你看一看核磁共振上的这个部位。

sentences.en: It looks like you have a tumor in your spinal cord.
sentences.zh: 看起来你的脊髓里长了个肿瘤。

sentences.en: A tumor.
sentences.zh: 一个肿瘤。

sentences.en: Not a bruise or a fracture, but something else entirely.
sentences.zh: 不是瘀伤或骨折，而是完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: There was, in the contrast, there was a lump inside of his spinal cord and his cervical spine, which is up near your neck.
sentences.zh: 通过造影对比，在他的脊髓和颈椎内部有一个肿块，颈椎就是靠近你脖子的部位。

sentences.en: And they said, this is inside, and it's very large, and it really needs to come out.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这个东西在里面，而且非常大，真的必须取出来。

sentences.en: Instantly, this explained everything.
sentences.zh: 瞬间，这一切都有了解释。

sentences.en: The joint pain, Colin's balance issues, his fatigue.
sentences.zh: 关节痛、科林的平衡问题、他的疲劳。

sentences.en: It was cancer.
sentences.zh: 那是癌症。

sentences.en: And it was almost too late.
sentences.zh: 而且几乎已经太迟了。

sentences.en: What was revealed to us was even more dire.
sentences.zh: 向我们揭示的情况甚至更加严峻。

sentences.en: You know, they said, had it been, as it was growing, had it been just another few millimeters further,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们说，要是再大一点，随着它生长，要是再往前长短短几毫米，

sentences.en: he would have already, it would have affected his ability to breathe.
sentences.zh: 他当时就已经，这会影响他的呼吸能力了。

sentences.en: So, let's think about that train ride again.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们再次回想那次地铁之旅。

sentences.en: The brutal assault.
sentences.zh: 那场残忍的袭击。

sentences.en: Was it a tragedy?
sentences.zh: 这是一场悲剧？

sentences.en: Or was it the luckiest ride of his life?
sentences.zh: 还是他一生中最幸运的一次乘车？

sentences.en: It led to a life-saving diagnosis, but it came at great coSt.
sentences.zh: 它带来了一个挽救生命的诊断，但代价也极其沉重。

sentences.en: In a situation like this, does the good outweigh the bad?
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，好处是否大于坏处？

sentences.en: Can bad ever come to be seen as good?
sentences.zh: 坏事有没有可能最终被看作是好事？

sentences.en: When I contacted Kristen Smith, the witness for the story,
sentences.zh: 当我联系到克里斯汀·史密斯——这个故事的目击者时，

sentences.en: I discovered she wasn't aware of what had happened to Colin and Lori after the attack.
sentences.zh: 我发现她并不知道袭击发生后科林和洛瑞怎么样了。

sentences.en: The story was hard for Kristen to hear, in part because her uncle had just died of a brain tumor.
sentences.zh: 克里斯汀很难接受这个故事，部分原因是因为她的叔叔刚刚死于脑瘤。

sentences.en: It was also such a quick thing.
sentences.zh: 这也是一件发生得太快的事。

sentences.en: We found out he was sick only maybe two and a half, three months ago, and now he's gone.
sentences.zh: 我们发现他生病大概也才两个半到三个月前，现在他已经走了。

sentences.en: And it's crazy to think that maybe if he had been attacked on a metro,
sentences.zh: 一想到如果他当时是在地铁上遭到袭击，

sentences.en: they would have caught it sooner and stopped it.
sentences.zh: 他们可能就会更早发现并阻止病情，这就太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I don't know, it's all just so strange.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，这一切都太诡异了。

sentences.en: But as the information sank in, Kristen began to reframe the way she viewed the attack on Colin.
sentences.zh: 但随着这些信息沉淀下来，克里斯汀开始重新看待她对科林遭遇袭击的看法。

sentences.en: I think something good did come from it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得确实从中产生了一些好事。

sentences.en: But I'm still left with the feeling of maybe even, well, no, I guess that's not true.
sentences.zh: 但我心里还是有一种感觉，甚至，好吧，不对，我想那不是真的。

sentences.en: If I had stopped the attack sooner, I was thinking he probably still would have gone to the hospital
sentences.zh: 如果我早点制止袭击，我在想他大概还是会去医院，

sentences.en: and they still would have found the tumor.
sentences.zh: 他们也还是会发现那个肿瘤。

sentences.en: But maybe that's not true.
sentences.zh: 但也许并非如此。

sentences.en: Maybe he had to be hurt to a degree that they really were investigating him deeply to find the tumor.
sentences.zh: 也许他必须受创到一定程度，他们才会对他进行深入检查从而发现肿瘤。

sentences.en: Exactly one month after being attacked on the train, Colin underwent a dangerous and difficult surgery
sentences.zh: 在火车上遇袭整整一个月后，科林接受了一台危险而艰难的手术，

sentences.en: to remove the cancerous tumor in his spine.
sentences.zh: 以切除他脊椎里的癌症肿瘤。

sentences.en: By most measures, it was a huge success.
sentences.zh: 从大多数标准来看，这是一次巨大的成功。

sentences.en: Colin survived and he wasn't paralyzed, which was something the doctors feared might happen.
sentences.zh: 科林活了下来，而且没有瘫痪，而这正是医生们担心可能会发生的情况。

sentences.en: But he was very far from his old self.
sentences.zh: 但他离恢复以前的自己还相去甚远。

sentences.en: I felt like my legs were floating in space, like several inches up from the bed and several inches over to the right,
sentences.zh: 我觉得我的双腿悬浮在太空中，距离床面向上好几英寸，向右偏了好几英寸，

sentences.en: which I thought was an amusing sensation at first, although I quickly didn't like that one.
sentences.zh: 起初我还觉得这是一种有趣的感官体验，尽管我很快就开始讨厌这种感觉了。

sentences.en: What soon became clear is that while he was able to move his body
sentences.zh: 不久之后显现出来的是，虽然他能够移动身体，

sentences.en: and feel heat, cold and some strange electrical twinges,
sentences.zh: 并且能感受到冷热和一些奇怪的电流刺痛感，

sentences.en: large parts of his body were numb.
sentences.zh: 但他身体的大片区域依然麻木。

sentences.en: Other parts of his body were wracked by endless pain.
sentences.zh: 身体的其他部位则饱受无休止疼痛的折磨。

sentences.en: And that's difficult when he, even taking a shower,
sentences.zh: 这就很痛苦了，当他，甚至只是洗个澡，

sentences.en: feeling the water on his body will cause him to scream.
sentences.zh: 感觉到水流过身体都会让他痛得尖叫。

sentences.en: And my son's bedroom is next to the shower.
sentences.zh: 而我儿子的卧室就在浴室旁边。

sentences.en: And that's difficult for the family, just empathizing with his pain.
sentences.zh: 这对家人来说也很艰难，只能对他的痛苦感同身受。

sentences.en: So this is where the Dales are now.
sentences.zh: 戴尔一家现在就是这个情况。

sentences.en: They're struggling to recover and make sense of a series of troubling and intertwined events.
sentences.zh: 他们正在艰难地康复，并试图理清一连串令人困扰且交织在一起的事件。

sentences.en: When I first heard about Colin and Laurie and the strange path to his diagnosis,
sentences.zh: 当我第一次听说科林和洛瑞以及他确诊的奇异经历时，

sentences.en: I, the outsider, immediately thought of the train attack as a blessing in disguise.
sentences.zh: 作为局外人的我，立刻把这起地铁袭击看作是“塞翁失马，焉知非福”。

sentences.en: Our witness, Kristen, had a more nuanced view, tinted by her own actions that day.
sentences.zh: 我们的目击者克里斯汀则有更细致的看法，这夹杂着她当天自身行为的影响。

sentences.en: As for Laurie, she says she tries to see the good in what happened.
sentences.zh: 至于洛瑞，她说她试着从发生的事情中看到积极的一面。

sentences.en: She mentions unexpected moments of kindness she encountered,
sentences.zh: 她提到了她遇到的那些意料之外的善意时刻，

sentences.en: like the time a school crossing guard, a stranger, dropped off a meal on her porch.
sentences.zh: 比如有一次，一个学校的交通协管员——一个陌生人，在她的门廊放下一顿饭。

sentences.en: But for Laurie and Colin, what happened on the train is still a recurring trauma.
sentences.zh: 但对于洛瑞和科林来说，火车上发生的事仍然是一场挥之不去的创伤。

sentences.en: That's really hard because, you know, there's a sense of reliving it every day.
sentences.zh: 这真的很艰难，因为，你知道的，那种每天都在重温经历的感觉。

sentences.en: When you go every day to the same spot and get on the train at the same spot
sentences.zh: 当你每天都去同一个地方，在同一个地方上车，

sentences.en: where your husband was lying down in his blood on his backpack.
sentences.zh: 而那里曾是你丈夫躺在血泊中的背包上的地方。

sentences.en: Did it have any silver linings at all?
sentences.zh: 这真的有什么好的一面吗？

sentences.en: Everyone, you know, everyone refers to what happened to Colin.
sentences.zh: 每个人，你知道的，每个人都会提到科林遭遇的事。

sentences.en: Oh, well, you got your diagnosis and you got the cancer out.
sentences.zh: 哦，你看，你确诊了，癌症也切除了。

sentences.en: What a silver lining.
sentences.zh: 多么因祸得福啊。

sentences.en: We're like, well, we sure would have hoped that that could have been diagnosed earlier in some other way.
sentences.zh: 我们就会想，好吧，我们当然希望当初能通过其他方式更早地诊断出来。

sentences.en: It's not the most ideal way to have that diagnosed, but we're glad that he's alive and has a good,
sentences.zh: 这不是确诊最理想的方式，但我们很高兴他还活着，而且有一个很好的，

sentences.en: I mean, he, they, the, what can we say?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他，他们，这个，我们能说什么呢？

sentences.en: That cancer is out.
sentences.zh: 那个癌症被切除了。

sentences.en: It doesn't seem to be growing, it doesn't seem to be growing back.
sentences.zh: 它似乎没有在生长，似乎也没有复发。

sentences.en: He has a positive, a relatively positive outlook.
sentences.zh: 他有着积极的，相对积极的心态。

sentences.en: So I can't help but think that you wouldn't have gotten that scan done when you did if it hadn't been for the incident.
sentences.zh: 所以我忍不住在想，要不是发生了那起事件，你当时是不会去做那个扫描的。

sentences.en: But the incident was truly horrible.
sentences.zh: 但那起事件确实太可怕了。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I don't know how to process that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么消化这件事。

sentences.en: You and me both.
sentences.zh: 我和你一样。

sentences.en: I asked Colin how he views what happened.
sentences.zh: 我问科林他是怎么看待这件事的。

sentences.en: Colin's considered the many ways of seeing what's happened.
sentences.zh: 科林考虑过看待这件事的多种方式。

sentences.en: Was it coincidence?
sentences.zh: 这是巧合吗？

sentences.en: The intervention of a higher power?
sentences.zh: 是某种更高力量的干预？

sentences.en: Luck?
sentences.zh: 是运气？

sentences.en: For now, Colin says, the frame of understanding that feels most right to him is simply acknowledging that life is random.
sentences.zh: 科林说，就目前而言，让他觉得最合适的理解框架，仅仅是承认生活是随机的。

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: There's a lot of things about this story that just line up almost too perfectly.
sentences.zh: 这个故事里有很多事情，几乎完美得有些过头了。

sentences.en: If this was an episode of a TV show, you'd be like, yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 如果这是一集电视剧，你大概会觉得：行吧，真敢编。

sentences.en: Yeah, I get it.
sentences.zh: 对，我懂。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I do like the random in many ways.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，我其实挺喜欢这种随机性的。

sentences.en: That sort of makes my universe more comfortable.
sentences.zh: 这某种程度上让我的宇宙感觉更舒适一些。

sentences.en: And maybe that's the most powerful truth in this tale.
sentences.zh: 也许这才是这个故事中最有力真相。

sentences.en: We all see things through our own lens, and we settle on the vision that gives us the greatest sense of comfort.
sentences.zh: 我们都透过自己的镜头看待事物，并倾向于那些能带给我们最大心理慰藉的视角。

sentences.en: When things happen to us, we sift and re-sift information to shape how we see the world.
sentences.zh: 当事情发生在我们身上时，我们会筛选并反复筛选信息，来塑造我们对世界的看法。

sentences.en: Imagine a group of people sitting around a campfire.
sentences.zh: 想象有一群人围坐在篝火旁。

sentences.en: One might see the fire as beautiful, the flames perhaps sparking memories of childhood and family and friends.
sentences.zh: 一个人可能会觉得火很美，火焰或许会勾起对童年、家人和朋友的回忆。

sentences.en: Another person, who'd suffered serious burn injuries, might see the very same fire as ugly and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 另一个人如果曾遭受严重烧伤，可能会觉得这同一场火既丑陋又危险。

sentences.en: There's no one reality.
sentences.zh: 世上并没有单一的现实。

sentences.en: It's all in the framing.
sentences.zh: 一切全在于如何解读。

sentences.en: As for the Dales, long before Colin's train assault and tumor, the family had planned a trip, a walking tour across the whole of England from coast to coast,
sentences.zh: 至于戴尔一家，早在科林遭遇列车袭击和肿瘤之前，全家就计划好了一次旅行，一次从东海岸到西海岸横穿整个英国的徒步之旅，

sentences.en: 260 miles on a rugged trail.
sentences.zh: 在一条崎岖的小路上走260英里。

sentences.en: They couldn't cancel, so they decided to go for it, despite everything that had happened.
sentences.zh: 他们无法取消，所以决定排除万难去完成它。

sentences.en: And the lore is that you pick up a stone from the west coast, and you walk it across, and then you put it in the east coast when you go to the other side.
sentences.zh: 按照传统，你要从西海岸捡起一块石头，把它一路带过去，当你走到另一边时，再把它放在东海岸。

sentences.en: And why do you carry a rock from west to east?
sentences.zh: 为什么要从西到东背一块石头呢？

sentences.en: What's the story?
sentences.zh: 这里面有什么讲究？

sentences.en: I think it just shows that you've made it.
sentences.zh: 我想这只是表明你成功完成了挑战。

sentences.en: You know, it's just a symbolic gesture to mark the end of that journey.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这只是一个标志着那段旅程结束的象征性举动。

sentences.en: For Colin, of course, this will be a milestone in his recovery, a chance to think.
sentences.zh: 当然，对科林来说，这将是他康复过程中的一个里程碑，也是一个思考的机会。

sentences.en: Because the way we see something isn't always how it really is.
sentences.zh: 因为我们看待事物的方式并不总是它真实的模样。

sentences.en: This week's episode was produced and edited by Jenny Schmidt.
sentences.zh: 本周的节目由珍妮·施密特制作和剪辑。

sentences.en: Our staff also includes Maggie Penman, Chris Benderev, Kara McGurk-Allison, and Renee Klar.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作人员还包括玛吉·彭曼、克里斯·本德列夫、卡拉·麦格克-艾莉森和蕾妮·克拉尔。

sentences.en: Our supervising producer is Tara Boyle.
sentences.zh: 我们的主管制作人是塔拉·博伊尔。

sentences.en: Last week, we began acknowledging the unsung heroes who are vital to the success of this show, but aren't typically in the credits.
sentences.zh: 上周，我们开始向那些对本节目成功至关重要、但通常不会出现在职员表中的幕后英雄致谢。

sentences.en: This week, our unsung hero is Nikala Matthews.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们的幕后英雄是尼卡拉·马修斯。

sentences.en: Nikala sits right near the Hidden Brain staff here at NPR, and she's become something of an honorary team member.
sentences.zh: 尼卡拉的座位就在NPR这里《隐藏的大脑》工作人员附近，她已经成了我们荣誉团队的一员。

sentences.en: She helps us reach new audiences through Facebook and Twitter, and we so appreciate her creative and collegial spirit.
sentences.zh: 她通过脸书和推特帮助我们接触新的受众，我们非常感激她极具创意和团结精神的工作态度。

sentences.en: Thanks, Nikala.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，尼卡拉。

sentences.en: Speaking of Facebook and Twitter, you can find more of my reporting on social media,
sentences.zh: 说到脸书和推特，你可以在社交媒体上找到更多我的报道，

sentences.en: along with great videos and animations that bring to life the research we highlight on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 以及生动展现我们在《隐藏的大脑》中重点关注的研究的出色视频和动画。

sentences.en: Check them out, and while you're there, we'd love it if you would share this episode and our stories
sentences.zh: 去看看吧，顺便一提，如果你能把这一集节目和我们的故事分享给

sentences.en: with friends who you think would enjoy our show.
sentences.zh: 你认为会喜欢我们节目的朋友，我们会非常高兴。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆，这里是NPR。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。
